title: AEO Certification, Tiering, and Lifecycle Management

qa_pairs.question: Which instrument introduced the multi-tiered (Tier 1-3) system for Authorized Economic Operators in Bangladesh?
qa_pairs.explanation: The AEO (Recognition and Operation) Rules 2024, referenced as being introduced in June 2024 and codified/operationalized in February 2025, established the tiered (1-3) system.

qa_pairs.question: What was the validity period of an Authorized Economic Operator recognition certificate according to the 2024 rules?
qa_pairs.explanation: According to the AEO (Recognition and Operation) Rules 2024 (as cited on 2024-06-13 and 2025-02-16), the recognition certificate is valid for a period of one year.

qa_pairs.question: When were the formal procedures for transitioning legacy entities to Tier-1 status and handling business changes refined?
qa_pairs.explanation: The Standing Order dated 2025-01-21 specifically refined renewal, business change protocols, and the transition of legacy entities to Tier-1 status.

qa_pairs.question: Under the 2025 operationalization of the AEO rules, what is the maximum time extension allowed for a Tier-1 entity to meet compliance conditions?
qa_pairs.explanation: Form-D (dated 2025-02-17) indicates that an entity may apply for a time extension of up to 6 months to fulfill Tier-1 compliance conditions.

qa_pairs.scenario: A company was granted AEO status under the 2018 Rules. Following the introduction of the 2024 Rules, the company is now classified as a Tier-1 entity but needs additional time to meet the new compliance conditions associated with this specific tier.
qa_pairs.question: Under the current operational framework established in 2025, what is the maximum extension of time the company can request to fulfill the Tier-1 compliance requirements, and which previous regulatory framework is referenced in their application?
qa_pairs.answer: The company may request an extension of up to 6 months, and the application references the Authorized Economic Operator (Recognition) Rules, 2018.

qa_pairs.scenario: An entity held an AEO certificate issued under the 2018 rules. With the transition to the 2024-2025 multi-tiered system, the entity is now being evaluated for its status under the new Tiered framework.
qa_pairs.question: How did the consequences of having a certificate revoked change between the 2018 Rules and the 2025 operationalization of the 2024 Rules regarding the ability to reapply?
qa_pairs.answer: Both the 2018 Rules and the 2025 operationalized 2024 Rules maintain a prohibition on reapplying for a new certificate for a set number of years from the date of revocation.

qa_pairs.question: Starting from the baseline AEO Rules 2018, what significant structural change to the AEO system was introduced six years later?
qa_pairs.answer: In June 2024, the AEO Rules 2024 were introduced, which transitioned the system from a single-tier status to a multi-tiered framework consisting of Tier 1-3 and Logistics Operator categories, along with formal application and renewal protocols.

qa_pairs.question: Following the 2024 AEO Rules implemented in mid-2024, what specific operational details were further formalized eight months later?
qa_pairs.answer: By February 2025 (specifically February 17, 2025), the AEO (Recognition and Operation) Rules 2024 were operationalized to include standardized forms for all lifecycle stages, specific audit requirements, and a defined classification structure for promotion to Tier-3 status.
